blocks.orig: You want to go on a safari, but don’t want to go by yourself? With this five day group tour, you can make your wildest dreams come true AND make new friends for life!
blocks.html: Dreaming of a safari, but not keen on travelling alone? On this five day group tour you can live out your wildest dreams AND meet friends for life!

blocks.orig: On the first Wednesday of every month, we pick up our travellers, aka you, at their hotel in Arusha. With a group of minimum three and maximum six people per jeep, you start your safari adventure then and there.
blocks.html: Every month on the first Wednesday, we collect our travellers, that is you, from their hotel in Arusha. With at least three and no more than six people in each jeep, your safari adventure begins right there.

blocks.orig: After meeting the grey giants of the Tarangire National Park on knee-level, you travel to the (in)famous Serengeti, where the Big Five and the Great Wildebeest Migration are waiting for you. The Ngorongoro Crater welcomes you afterwards with both, out-of-this-world nature and the world’s highest concentration of wildlife.
blocks.html: First you meet the grey giants of Tarangire National Park at knee height, then you head on to the (in)famous Serengeti, where the Great Wildebeest Migration and the Big Five await. Afterwards the Ngorongoro Crater greets you with otherworldly scenery as well as the highest concentration of wildlife in the world.

blocks.orig: Between these unforgettable moments, you relax in authentic lodges which pamper you with Tanzanian hospitality, a cosy single room and delicious cuisine. Sit together with your fellow travellers, watch the glowing red sun setting at the horizon, and raise your glass to new memories. These are the most experience-packed five days of your life – and they will stay with you forever.
blocks.html: In between these unforgettable moments you unwind in authentic lodges that spoil you with Tanzanian hospitality, a comfortable single room and tasty food. Join your fellow travellers, watch the glowing red sun go down on the horizon and raise a glass to new memories. These five days are packed with more experiences than any others in your life, and they will stay with you for ever.

blocks.orig: We confirm each trip no later than 20 days before departure. If fewer than three participants are registered by then, the trip will not take place. In that case, you may cancel your booking with us (and, if you wish, join another provider’s trip on the same dates) or postpone your trip.
blocks.html: Every trip is confirmed at the latest 20 days ahead of departure. Should fewer than three participants have signed up by that date, the trip does not go ahead. You can then cancel your booking with us (and, if you like, join a trip run by another provider on the same dates) or move your trip to a later date.

blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is well known for its big groups of elephants and the huge amount of giant baobab trees. These trees can live for hundreds of years and are actually a source of water for elephants in the dry season as they have a special technique to draw water from them. Besides, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why in this season in Tarangire you can see groups of up to 250 elephants next to many more animals!
blocks.html: Tarangire National Park is famous for its big elephant herds and the large number of giant baobab trees. The baobabs can live for several hundred years, and during the dry season they actually provide elephants with water, thanks to a special technique the elephants use to draw it out. In addition, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why you can then see herds of up to 250 elephants in Tarangire, alongside many more animals!

blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park is widely known as the place to go on safari, mainly because of the Great Migration that passes through here. The enormous, stampeding herds are impressive, as are the vast number of predators that live here: over four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas, and hundreds of wild dogs! And of course, plenty of other beautiful animals, which your guide will be delighted to search for together with you. Are you ready for this?
blocks.html: Serengeti National Park is well known as the safari destination, largely because the Great Migration passes through it. The massive stampeding herds make a big impression, as does the huge number of predators that live here: more than four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas and hundreds of wild dogs! And naturally there are plenty of other beautiful animals, which your guide will gladly look for together with you. Are you ready?

blocks.orig: From late December through March, the Ndutu region becomes the heart of the Great Migration, as over 2 million animals arrive to give birth. The Ndutu region straddles the southern part of the Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. The short, nutrient-rich grass makes the area a haven for newborn zebras and wildebeests, but also a prime spot for predators. This seasonal gathering creates close-up wildlife sightings and constant activity across the plains.
blocks.html: Between late December and March, the Ndutu region forms the heart of the Great Migration, with more than 2 million animals arriving to give birth. Ndutu spans the southern Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Thanks to the short grass, packed with nutrients, it is a safe place for newborn wildebeests and zebras, and at the same time an excellent spot for predators. This seasonal gathering means close-up sightings and nonstop activity on the plains.

blocks.orig: The famous Ngorongoro Crater is one of Africa's seven natural wonders. The crater was formed two million years ago when a vast volcano erupted. The fertile lava has created a unique ecosystem, now home to the highest concentration of animals found anywhere in Africa! Once in the crater, thousands of animals such as lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos surround you, and the views are astounding – you won’t know where to look!
blocks.html: The well-known Ngorongoro Crater ranks as one of Africa's seven natural wonders. It took shape two million years ago when a massive volcano erupted. The fertile lava produced a unique ecosystem that is now home to Africa's highest concentration of animals! Inside the crater, thousands of animals, including lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos, are all around you, and the views are so remarkable you won’t know where to look!

blocks.orig: Sadly, this is the last day of your safari. Enjoy the last few hours of your holiday before our driver brings you back to Arusha.
blocks.html: Unfortunately, today is the final day of your safari. Make the most of your last hours on holiday until our driver takes you back to Arusha.
